newsitem.title: CHINA: China angered by Taiwan official's Indonesia visit.
newsitem.headline: China angered by Taiwan official's Indonesia visit.

text.p: China said on Friday it had made serious representations with Indonesia for hosting the foreign minister of its arch-rival, Taiwan.
Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas has confirmed that he met his Taiwan counterpart, John Chang, in Jakarta on Wednesday, but stressed that he had done so in his private capacity.

"The Chinese government has made serious representations with the Indonesian government over its permitting John Chang ... to visit Indonesia and arranging meetings with high-level Indonesian officials," the Xinhua news agency quoted China's Foreign Ministry spokesman, Shen Guofang, as saying.
Chang is a grandson of the late Nationalist leader Chiang Kai-shek, who fled to Taiwan in 1949 after the defeat of his armies by the communists in the Chinese civil war.
Beijing has regarded Taiwan as a rebel province since then and has tried to isolate the island diplomatically.

"China is steadfastly opposed to any country which has diplomatic relations with it forming official ties with Taiwan or having official exchanges and contacts with it in whatever form," Shen was quoted as saying.
"China hopes Indonesia will treasure the existing good-neighbourly and friendly ties between the two countries," Shen said.
Indonesian Foreign Ministry sources said Chang had met Research and Technology Minister Jusuf Habibie and was scheduled to call on President Suharto. It was not known if Chang actually met Suharto.
Chang's trip to Indonesia followed Taiwan Vice President Lien Chan's secret visit to the former Soviet republic of Ukraine last month.
Taiwanese President Lee Teng-hui made an unofficial visit to Indonesia in February 1994. China was enraged and protested to Jakarta.
